endorsements.quote: LLM-PROMs will need to be developed with multi-stakeholder input and careful validation against established PROMs.
Integrating patient organizations at the core of these developments will be a key factor ensuring that LLM-PROMs actually foster patient-centered care.

unlisted_practices: Rigorously test LLM-PROMs for objectivity, reliability, validity, and responsiveness before clinical use, using existing PROMs as the gold standard for convergent validity and proving predictive validity and responsiveness.
Evaluate the administration burden of LLM-PROMs before implementing them in routine health care delivery.
Use heterogeneous training sets for AI models that reflect the populations in which LLM-PROMs are intended to be used (e.g., sex, age, ethnicity).
Develop a separate safety filter network that detects inappropriate LLM-PROM items before they are displayed to the respondent and corrects for biases.
Use knowledge from existing PROMs to develop application-specific vocabularies and safety control mechanisms for LLM-PROMs.
Demonstrate LLM-PROM interaction with electronic health records before integrating them into clinical care pathways.

screen.reason: This is a short commentary discussing the potential and governance/validation considerations of using large language models for patient-reported outcome measures (LLM-PROMs).
